LESSON: DIRECT SOWING OF TINY SEEDS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested
Topic 2.1: Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does direct sowing of tiny seeds enhance food production process?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DIRECT SOWING OF TINY SEEDS
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds

What this means
In this part you learn to identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds” around your school. (skill: identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does direct sowing of tiny seeds enhance food production process?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Direct Sowing of Tiny Seeds means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify crops established through direct sowing of tiny seeds.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
